clue.text: Ancient relic restaurant patron spotted, some say

indicators.note: 'some say' tells us the phrase before it is to be spoken, and only its sound counts

parts.note: a restaurant patron is a diner, and spotted is saw

explanation.surface: Someone claims an elderly regular was seen dining at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, DINER SAW sounds like DINOSAUR. 'Ancient relic' hints at an old-timer, but here it is the fossil creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs are prehistoric creatures known from fossils, the oldest of remains; the word also mocks anyone hopelessly old-fashioned.

clue.text: Nervous away from the centre

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tense and jumpy
second meaning, read literally: out at the edge

explanation.surface: Someone feels anxious when pushed out to the margins.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful literal reading: something out towards an edge rather than the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy commonly means tense or on edge, and can be read as lying on the periphery, near a border.

clue.text: Chopstick?

parts.note: surface reading: an eating utensil used in East Asia
setter's reading: split the word in two, a verb meaning both to chop and to stick

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks you to break the word apart: one verb famously means both to split and to adhere, opposite senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split with a heavy blow, and also, in older usage, to adhere firmly or remain loyal.

clue.text: Dressing up to do a sort of calypso

indicators.note: doing a sort of version of something means producing a rearranged form of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People put on costumes to perform a version of a Caribbean song.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosplay is the hobby of wearing costumes to impersonate characters from films, comics or games.

clue.text: Little star, one doing a turn round Malaysian capital

indicators.note: going round something means wrapping around it, enclosing it

parts.note: to twine is to twist or wind, so one who does it
KL is the usual short form of Kuala Lumpur

explanation.surface: A young performer spinning around Kuala Lumpur is a rising star.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Twinkle, twinkle, little star' makes 'Little star' a playful definition rather than a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinkler is something that twinkles, as stars do in the rhyme sung to children.

clue.text: Opposing the regime, native is to suffer

indicators.note: letters made to suffer are knocked about and fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A local dissident must endure hardship for resisting the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hostile to the Soviet Union's government means standing against that particular communist regime.

clue.text: One far off? Absolutely not

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether a distant person is gone, with a firm denial.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No fear!' is an informal British exclamation of emphatic refusal, meaning certainly not.

clue.text: Old boy back on the Bordeaux with nothing for a hot meal

parts.note: Bordeaux is a wine, French vin

indicators.note: going back means the phrase for an old boy is read from right to left

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a boy is a lad
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A retired gentleman returns to his claret with nothing to eat but a fiery curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' looks like one unit meaning a former pupil, but it splits into two pieces before being turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a very spicy Indian curry, a classic hot dish.

clue.text: Press home one's advantage, or scatter to the winds

definitions.meaning: first reading, split as two words: take victory at once
second meaning: blow chaff away from grain

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense works only when the answer is split as WIN NOW; the second is the farming verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To winnow is to toss grain so the wind carries off the husks, separating it out.

clue.text: A rarely pretentious bunch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an uncommon spelling of posey, showy
second meaning: a small bouquet of flowers

explanation.surface: A group of people who are, unusually, not showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' looks like 'seldom', but says the spelling for pretentious is a rare variant of posey.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bouquet; posey, also spelt this way occasionally, means affected or showy.

clue.text: Extra material in university course, and taking that is killing for an American

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, here the course inside the joining word

parts.note: taken as written
Politics, Philosophy and Economics, an Oxford degree

parts.words: that is killing for an American
parts.note: in US slang to ice someone is to kill them

explanation.surface: Extra reading in a degree course, plus something about a murder in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own 'and' is used as letters, with the course sitting inside it. PPE is a well-known British degree combining politics, philosophy and economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendices are supplementary sections at the back of a book or report, holding additional material.

clue.text: Caution packing a fine flask

indicators.note: packing something means holding it inside, like goods in a case

parts.note: caution is care
taken as written
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Take care when packing a delicate bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass vessel with a wide mouth for serving wine or water, a kind of bottle.

clue.text: No ordinary people get good luck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: only the finest, the elite
second meaning: a farewell wish

explanation.surface: Only the elite are fortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common parting wish for success, and can also literally name the finest individuals as a group.

clue.text: Upon which rabbit departs, his innings involving no runs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hands and feet a running animal uses
second meaning: a cricket score made entirely from boundaries

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a rabbit is a hopeless batter and a four is a boundary hit, scored without running; so an innings of only fours needs no running.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on hands and knees is being on all fours, and a cricket innings made solely of boundary fours is jokingly all fours.

clue.text: Being repeatedly exercised made a bore

definitions.meaning: first meaning: trained by repetition, as soldiers are
second meaning: bored a hole

explanation.surface: Endless practice turned someone tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is a hole made by a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are drilled on the parade ground, and a hole is drilled with a bit; both senses fit.

clue.text: Basic principles of the weather

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rudiments of a subject
second meaning: wind, rain and storms

explanation.surface: Fundamentals of meteorology.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements of a subject are its rudiments, and exposure to the elements means exposure to wind and rain.

clue.text: A weakness for a woman's name in Shakespeare?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a moral failing
second meaning: Hamlet addresses this quality as being called 'woman'

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says 'Frailty, thy name is woman!', so in Shakespeare woman is its name, reversed playfully here.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailty is weakness of body or character, a lack of strength or resolve.

clue.text: Line of verse neat and safe but lacking power

indicators.note: lacking power means the letter for power, P, is dropped

parts.note: neat is trim
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A tidy and secure line, though it lacks force.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old thieves' slang for a safe, and P is the usual abbreviation for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimeter is a line of poetry with three metrical feet.

clue.text: Perhaps fine writer always includes regular characters in plot

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool, here the writer

indicators.note: includes means one word takes another inside it

parts.note: ay is an old and poetic word for ever

indicators.note: regular characters are every other letter, picked at even intervals

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A novelist keeps putting stock characters into the storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a fine is only one example of the answer, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine is one kind of punishment, so it is an example of a punitive sanction.

clue.text: Cream she churned, product of a goat

indicators.note: churned means stirred vigorously, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer churns cream from her goat's milk.
explanation.walkthrough: Churned cream suggests butter or cheese from goat's milk, but the product is wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine soft wool from the undercoat of Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Keep performing, securing a single engagement

indicators.note: securing something means holding it firmly inside

parts.note: to act on is to keep acting, carry on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An actor carries on working after landing a one-off booking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' looks like a theatre booking in this scene, but it is a military clash.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers in action are fighting; an engagement is a battle with the enemy.

clue.text: Knight, seized from behind by murderer, that hangs from a tree

indicators.note: something seized is held tight inside another's grasp

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

indicators.note: read from behind means taken from the end backwards

parts.note: KT is the abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is grabbed from behind by a killer and left hanging from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A catkin is the dangling spike of tiny flowers on trees such as willow and hazel.

clue.text: Like the side of the face to be forward?

definitions.text: Like the side of the face
definitions.meaning: first meaning: relating to the cheek
second meaning: impudent, presumptuous

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a jokey literal one, as if formed from cheek plus -y.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forward is bold and impertinent, which is what cheeky means in everyday speech.

clue.text: Working in black, draw companion

indicators.note: working in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: a chess game ending with no win is a stalemate
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Black pieces in a chess match end level, with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse from the same stable, so by extension a colleague or associate.

clue.text: Creepy obsessive for one writing avoiding unfamiliar alphabet

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out the letter for writing

parts.note: 'It's Greek to me' says something is unfamiliar
writing is one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A sinister fanatic avoids writing in a strange script.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of GREEK. Writing, reading and arithmetic are the three Rs of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A geek is an obsessive enthusiast; the earliest geeks were creepy carnival performers, so either kind is an example.

clue.text: Sellers for example don't stop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of a famous comic radio team
second meaning: two words, carry on

explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers was a star of The Goon Show, a 1950s BBC radio comedy. Sellers looks like shopkeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goons were the comedians of that radio show, and the split phrase GO ON urges someone to continue.

clue.text: Jazz trombonist has a year off for time in rural area

indicators.note: one thing off for another means it is removed and replaced

parts.note: Tommy Dorsey, American swing-era bandleader
Y is the abbreviation for year
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A jazz musician takes a year off to spend time in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the Y of DORSEY for T. Dorset is a largely rural county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is an English county known for farmland and coast, so it is a countryside region.

clue.text: Assume command to get into shelter doesn't include Charlie

parts.note: to take to or get into a habit

indicators.note: not including something means leaving that letter out

parts.note: shelter is cover
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An officer seizes control so the troops can get into a bunker, minus one soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To take over is to seize control or responsibility from someone else.
